5] This appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claima Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 16/01/2014 passed in Claim Case No.30/2012 by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar (M.P.) seeking enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
6] In brief, the facts of the case are that the husband of appellant No.1, father of appellant No.2 and son of appellant No.3 Mahesh Kumar died in an accident which took place on 30/04/2012.

The case of the claimants is that on the said date, the deceased was posted on deputation as a driver in the Commercial Tax Department of M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation Ltd., Dhar.

entities.text: M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation Ltd., Dhar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According the appellants, the deceased was drawing a salary of Rs.12,906/- per month and on 30/04/2012, at around 11:30 am, when the deceased was going to Dhar, at that time a bus bearing registration No.MP-11 K 1149 being driven by respondent No.1 Subhashchandra rashly and negligently dashed the deceased, as a result of which, he got injured and was taken to Shashkiya Bhoj Chikitsalaya, Dhar and from there to M.Y. Hospital, Indore where he succumbed to his injuries.

On account of his death, the appellants filed claim case No.30/2012 in the Court of Member, MACT, Dhar under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act which was decided on 16/01/2014 and the award of Rs.6,40,000/- with interest of 7.5% per annum from the date of application was awarded to the appellants and being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal has been preferred.

7] Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the learned Member of the Tribunal has erred in holding that the deceased Mahesh was earning a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month only despite the fact that his salary slip, certificate etc. Exhibit A/9 to A/11 were placed to prove on record by the claimants.

Counsel for the appellants has drawn the attention of this Court to to last salary drawn certificate dated 14/09/2012 of the deceased proved as Ex. A/10 in which the gross salary of the Smt. Kiran vs Subhashchandra on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79900447/
2 deceased is said to be Rs.12,906/-.

Counsel has also submitted that the service of the deceased were already regularized when he was in his parent department of the said federation regarding which Ex.A/11 has been proved through PW/5 Shakil Ahmed Siddhiqui, the Assistant Manager Incharge in the federation.

Thus, it is submitted that there was no reason for the learned Tribunal to hold that the deceased was earning only Rs.5,000/- per month and thus, the entire calculation has been made on that basis only.

Counsel has also submitted that the deceased was although posted on deputation in the Commercial Tax Department but under the contingency paid funds through order dated 18/01/2011 but that in itself is not sufficient to hold that the deceased was not a regular employee specially when Ex.A/11 has been proved in this behalf by the competent officer of the federation.

In support of his submission, Shri Himanshu, Paliwal, counsel for the appellants has relied upon the judgement passed in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) and in the case of Magma HDI Vs. Nanuram and others reported as 2018 ACJ 5 (SC).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma HDI Vs. Nanuram and others reported as 2018 ACJ 5 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the award be appropriately enhanced.
8] Counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the award is just and proper and no interference is called for.

9] Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10] From the record, it is found that only the point involved in the present case is that of the salary which the deceased Mahesh was earning at the time of accident which, according to the learned Member of the Tribunal was Rs.5,000/- only as the documents filed by the claimants Ex.A/8 to A/11 have been disbelieved on the ground that the deceased was employed on contingency basis and was not a regular employee and there is always a difference in the pay structure of contingency based employees and regular employees.

The Tribunal has also disbelieved the deposition of PW/5 Shakil Ahmed Siddhiqui who has proved Ex.A/11 in which the deceased is said to be a regular employee w.e.f. 01/05/1987, on the ground that this witness has clearly stated that the deceased was a contingency employee.

11] On close scrutiny of the documents filed by claimants as also the deposition of the witnesses, it is found that PW/3 G.D. Maheshwari, the Commercial Tax Officer has stated that the deceased was employed as a driver in their department on deputation.

He has also admitted that the deceased Mahesh Kumar Verma was employed under the contingency paid employee in his parent department i.e. M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation however, he has feigned ignorance as to what was his original salary in that department but what were the conditions of his employment.

entities.text: M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
12] So far as PW/5 Shakil Ahmed Siddhiqui is concerned who was posted as Assistant Manager,
In-charge of M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation, and has proved Ex.A/11 which is a certificate endorsing that the services of the deceased Mahesh were regularized w.e.f. 01/05/1987,
vide order No.Til/Karmik/87/10980/ Dated 06/05/1987.

entities.text: M.P. State Co-operative Oil Seed Growers Federation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: This witness has clearly stated that the deceased was employed in their department till 2009 and after that, he was sent on deputation to the Commercial Tax Department.
He has also clearly stated that the services of the deceased were regularized w.e.f. 01/05/1987.

3 13]

On due consideration of the aforesaid evidence on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that there was no reason for the learned Member of the Tribunal to discard or disbelieve the deposition of PW/5 who is an officer of the State owned federation.

This Court also finds that in the certificate of regularization Ex.A/11, the order reference number is also given along with the date and thus, in the absence of any other evidence to the contrary, it can be presumed under Section 114,
illustration(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that inter alia, the court may presume the existence of the fact that official acts have been regularly performed.

Otherwise also, this Court is of the considered opinion that the responsible officer of government federation would not give a false evidence in the Court where a claim has been made by the family members of the deceased employee who was posted as a driver.

It is true that there is a difference in the regular and contingency paid employees,
however, after the documents Ex.A/11 was filed by the respondent along with reference number of his regularization order, the onus was on the respondents to demonstrate by leading evidence that the aforesaid order was not in existence and in-fact in his cross examination, PW/5 Shakil Ahmed Siddhiqui was also asked if he has brought any record of the deceased, to which, he has stated that he has brought the service book of the deceased but it has not produced it in the Court, but the insurance company could not gather the courage to prove the aforesaid service book on record which they could have done at that time only, which only shows that the insurance company was also not sure about the suggestions which were given to this witness.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the finding arrived at by the claims Tribunal that the deceased was earning Rs.5,000/- despite the fact that he had produced the salary certificate in which his salary is stated to be Rs.12,906/-, is erroneous and need interference.

And the fact that he has also been able to prove that he was in regular service, this Court holds that the income of the deceased should be taken as Rs.12,906/- per month instead of Rs.5,000/- only and accordingly while applying the ratio in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pranay Sethi (supra) as also Magma HDI Vs. Nanuram (supra), this Court finds that the calculation can be made in the following manner:-
The calculation made by the claims Tribunal:-
 Dependency 5000 X 1/3 X 12 X 13 5,2  Funeral 10,
 Loss of love and affection to the child 5,
 Loss of consortium 1,0  Loss of love and affection to the mother 5,
 Total 6,4 After assessing the income of the deceased and other head:-
Dependency 12,906 + 30% = 16,777.80 - 1/3 = 17,44,891.20 5,592.60 = 11,185.20 X 12 = 134222.4 X 13 Consortium/filial 44,000 X 3 1,32,000 Loss of estate 16,500 Funeral 16,500 Total 19,09,891

14] In view of the above, the appal stands allowed and the appellants shall be entitled to receive an additional enhanced amount of Rs.12,69,891/- towards the Smt. Kiran vs Subhashchandra on 21 June, 2023

It is also directed that the Court fees be refunded back to the appellants which has been paid by them in accordance with law.
